nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be the left shift on the full 2-shift $X$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$. The aperiodic part of $X$ is the set of all $x \in X$ that are not periodic for $\sigma$, that is, with $\sigma^n x \ne x$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Aperiodic part of the full 2-shift

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be the left shift on the full 3-shift, given by $(\sigma y)_i = y_{i+1}$. The aperiodic part of the proper 3-colouring shift $Y$ is the set of all $y \in Y$ that are not periodic for $\sigma$, that is, with $\sigma^n y \ne y$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Aperiodic part of the 3-colouring shift

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be the full 2-shift, $Y$ the proper 3-colouring shift, and $\sigma$ the left shift on each. There is no homeomorphism $e$ from the aperiodic part of $X$ onto the aperiodic part of $Y$, each with the subspace topology, such that $e(\sigma a) = \sigma(e(a))$ for every $a$ in the aperiodic part of $X$; that is, Hochman's aperiodic conjugacy question has a negative answer.
nodes.title: The aperiodic parts of the full 2-shift and the 3-colouring shift are not conjugate

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be the full 2-shift and $Y$ the proper 3-colouring shift, write $X \setminus \mathrm{Per}(X)$ and $Y \setminus \mathrm{Per}(Y)$ for their aperiodic parts with the subspace topologies, and let $\sigma$ be the left shift $(\sigma z)_i = z_{i+1}$ on each. The statement is that there is a homeomorphism $e \colon X \setminus \mathrm{Per}(X) \to Y \setminus \mathrm{Per}(Y)$ with $e(\sigma a) = \sigma(e(a))$ for…
nodes.title: Hochman's aperiodic conjugacy question

nodes.summary: The left shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, maps the aperiodic part of the full 2-shift $X$ into itself; this is the self-map of the aperiodic part of $X$ obtained by restricting $\sigma$ to it.
nodes.title: Shift on the aperiodic part of the full 2-shift

nodes.summary: The left shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma y)_i = y_{i+1}$, maps the aperiodic part of the proper 3-colouring shift $Y$ into itself; this is the self-map of the aperiodic part of $Y$ obtained by restricting $\sigma$ to it.
nodes.title: Shift on the aperiodic part of the 3-colouring shift

nodes.summary: $X$ is the space of all two-sided sequences $x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with every $x_i \in \{0, 1\}$, carrying the product topology.
nodes.title: The full 2-shift

nodes.summary: $Y$ is the set of sequences $y = (y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ in the full 3-shift (so every $y_i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$) such that $y_i \ne y_{i+1}$ for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: The proper 3-colouring shift

nodes.summary: The space of all two-sided sequences $y = (y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ with every $y_i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, carrying the product topology. It is the ambient space of the proper 3-colouring shift.
nodes.title: The full 3-shift
